evals.prompt: I'm starting a new invoicing SaaS with Next.js, TypeScript and Postgres. Set up the repo properly before we write features.
evals.expected_output: A bootstrap plan in the skill's output format: Tier 1 items in the first PR (README, .gitignore with .env ignored, .env.example, .editorconfig, pinned Node version, lockfile, formatter, linter, strict tsconfig, pre-commit hooks, secret scanning, validated env module, standard task names with a check task, CI running check, branch protection, AGENTS.md, ADR-0001), a walking skeleton deployed by CI with /healthz and one smoke test, and Tier 2/3 items listed as TODOs.
expectations: CI is part of the first PR and runs the same check task developers run locally
tsconfig uses strict mode (strict: true)
Environment variables are validated in a single config module at startup and .env is not committed
A walking skeleton (route to API to DB, deployed by CI) comes before feature work
AGENTS.md and a first ADR are created
Tier 2 items such as error tracking and backups are listed as TODOs rather than silently skipped
Does not propose microservices or Kubernetes

evals.prompt: Our Django repo has no CI, no formatter, and people push straight to main. What should we fix first?
evals.expected_output: An audit table (item, present?, evidence, action) followed by a tier-ordered plan: CI running format check, lint, typecheck and tests with Ruff and a type checker; branch protection requiring PRs and passing checks; fast pre-commit hooks; secret scanning; validated settings; then Tier 2 items. Keeps the existing Django layout rather than re-scaffolding.
expectations: Starts from an audit of what exists rather than re-scaffolding the project
Recommends branch protection with required status checks on main
Recommends Ruff for formatting and linting and a type checker such as mypy or pyright
Keeps pre-commit hooks to fast checks and runs the test suite in CI
Orders the work by tier (day-one items before first-user and first-teammate items)

evals.prompt: We need an app with auth, projects, billing, notifications, reports and an admin panel. Scaffold all the modules, services and folders up front so the structure is ready.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on big-bang scaffolding: builds one feature end to end as a walking skeleton, deploys it through CI, then adds the next slice. Creates folders only for the first slice and keeps one deployable.
expectations: Recommends building one vertical slice end to end and deploying it before scaffolding other features
Does not create empty folders or services for features that are not being built yet
Keeps a single deployable (no microservices) for the new product
Explains the reason (walking skeleton, Gall's law, or cost of gold-plating)

evals.prompt: Should our new backend API be written in Go or Rust?
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: this is a stack decision, so it defers to tech-stack-selection (team skill, deployment target, criteria matrix) instead of producing a repo bootstrap checklist.
expectations: Does not produce the day-one repository checklist as the main answer
Frames the answer around stack-selection criteria such as team skill and requirements, or points to tech-stack-selection

evals.prompt: Set up preview environments per PR and a staging environment with separate secrets for our existing app.
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: environments and secrets depth belongs to environments-and-config and deployment-and-infrastructure; the answer defers or loads those skills rather than restating the bootstrap checklist.
expectations: Points to or uses environments-and-config or deployment-and-infrastructure for the environment and secrets design
Does not re-scaffold the repository or restart the bootstrap workflow
